newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA TO SHUT THREE OIL REFINERIES - PM.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA TO SHUT THREE OIL REFINERIES - PM.

text.p: Romania will shut three oil refineries to help liquidate loss-making companies, in line with suggestions made by international lenders, Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Wednesday.
"Starting today, supplies of electricity, crude oil and water will be cut to three refineries: Petrotel, Darmanesti and Vega," Ciorbea told a news conference.
Ciorbea said the country's 11 refineries were inefficient and generated huge losses for the economy.
"We must target the oil processing sector for restructuring," the prime minister said.

Ciorbea's announcement came at the end of a one-month visit by an International Monetary Fund mission which assessed Romania's reform progress. The move is also in line with recommendations made by the IMF in exchange for new credits.
The Petrotel SA refinery is located in the oilfield of Ploiesti and has a capacity of some one million tonnes per year.
The plant has a degree of conversion and secondary processing capacity comparable to Western plants, but with a poorer technical and economic performance.
The old Darmanesti SA refinery, in the eastern province of Moldova, also has a capacity of one million tonnes a year. It lacks crude feedstock flexibility.

The Vega SA refinery, with an operating capacity of 800,000 tonnes per year, has a low overall utilisation as its specialist products, including lubes, special catalysts and solvents are in low demand.
Romania has an oversized refining capacity of some 34 million tonnes a year, inherited from the former communist regime, which operates at a capacity of well over 20 million tonnes.
IMF chief negotiator for Romania Poul Thomsen said the government should step up efforts to restructure loss-making industries.
On Thursday, Bucharest radio said trade unions in the oil processing sector had threatened to start street protests against the government's plans to streamline the sector.
